title: Keeping a vocabulary notebook
subtitle: write down, translation, topic, tip
summary: Organise a vocabulary notebook by topic, and learn what to write next to each new word: a translation, an explanation, synonyms and an example sentence.

lesson.heading: What do students do?
lesson.text: Five students talk about their notebooks. To **write down** or **note down** a word means to write it so that you do not lose it. If you **make a note of** a word, you do the same thing. Many students add a **translation** - the same word in their own language.

examples.text: I **write down** new English words and phrases, and next to each one I write a Spanish **translation**.

examples.note: a mess = nothing is in a good order; a synonym is untidy

examples.text: I sometimes **make a note of** new words, but I often **forget**.
I **note down** new words and phrases, and sometimes I write an **explanation** in English.
examples.note: an explanation = a description of what something means

lesson.heading: Organise your words by topic
lesson.text: A **topic** is a subject, for example food, clothes or animals. Many students **list** their words by topic: all the animal words together, all the clothes words together. It is easier to remember them this way. Keep the topics apart and don't **mix them up**.

examples.text: I try and **list** words by **topic**, so I put all the animals together.
Put food in one place and clothes in another. Don't **mix them up**.
examples.note: mix up = put things together with no order

examples.text: Some words and phrases will go in more than one **topic**.

lesson.heading: Words with no topic
lesson.text: Some words, for example *useful* or *in particular*, do not belong to a topic. Put them in a different part of your notebook: a page for each day, each week, or each English lesson. Write the date clearly at the top.

examples.note: This is how we write the date at the top of a page.

lesson.heading: Translations and explanations
lesson.text: Write a **translation** if it is **necessary**, but also write the meaning in English if it is possible, or draw a picture. To **translate** a word is to put it into another language; the noun is **translation**.

examples.text: Sometimes I **translate** new words into Polish.
examples.note: You translate something into another language.
necessary = you need it; the opposite is unnecessary
This is an explanation in English, not a translation.

lesson.heading: What else can you write next to a word?
rows: a synonym (a word with a similar meaning)
awful = terrible; a synonym is dreadful
the opposite of forget is remember
the opposite of necessary is unnecessary
a tip is advice, and also money you give a waiter
I enjoy living in a big city.

lesson.heading: Example sentences and word partners
lesson.text: An example sentence helps you with the grammar of a word and with its **word partners** - the words that usually go with it. Word partners are also called **collocations**. Copy the sentence into your notebook.

examples.text: I **enjoy living** in a big city.
examples.wrong: I enjoy to live in a big city.
examples.note: enjoy is followed by an -ing form

examples.wrong: I passed two weeks in Rome.
examples.note: You spend time in a place.

lesson.heading: Tips
lesson.text: A **tip** is a piece of advice to help you. Remember that many words have more than one meaning that you need to know. A *tip* is also the money you give to a waiter for serving you in a restaurant.

examples.text: Here is a useful **tip**: write the date at the top of the page.
We left a **tip** for the waiter.
examples.note: tip = money you give for good service

lesson.text: Write the word, the meaning *and* an example sentence. One word with an example is worth more than three words on their own.

exercises.prompt: Put each word into the right topic.
This fish is ___, so we can't eat it yet.

options: a small garden behind a house
exercises.explanation: A butcher is a person who sells meat. This word goes in the food topic.

exercises.prompt: Before dinner I put the plates, knives and forks on the table. In other words, I ___ the table.
exercises.explanation: To lay the table = to put plates, knives, forks and so on on a table before a meal.
We say minus for the sign -, and this word belongs to the numbers topic.

exercises.prompt: Match each word with the extra information you can write next to it in your notebook.
I need this book for my exam, so a good dictionary is ___ too.
exercises.explanation: Necessary means you need it. The opposite is unnecessary.

exercises.prompt: The film was awful. In fact, it was the most ___ film I have ever seen.
exercises.explanation: Awful, dreadful and terrible are synonyms - they have a similar meaning.

exercises.statement: The word tip has only one meaning: a piece of advice.
exercises.explanation: Tip has two meanings: a piece of advice, and money you give a waiter for serving you.

options: I enjoy living in a big city.
I enjoy to live in a big city.
I enjoy live in a big city.
I enjoy that I live in a big city.
exercises.explanation: Enjoy is followed by an -ing form, so an example sentence helps you with the grammar.

exercises.prompt: I ___ two weeks in Rome last summer.
exercises.explanation: You spend time in a place - spend is the word partner of time.

exercises.prompt: Keep the food words on one page and the clothes words on another. Don't ___ them up.
exercises.hint: (= put them together with no order)
exercises.explanation: To mix words up is to put them together with no order.

exercises.prompt: How does Donata use her notebook?
exercises.answer: I note down new words and phrases in my notebook.
exercises.explanation: Note down and write down mean the same thing.
